scenes.say: Most AI apps use a writing machine to answer yes or no questions. Google just built one that can't write at all.
Say your app gets a thousand support emails. For each one, it needs three answers. Is it angry? Is it urgent? Who should handle it?
Today, the app asks a chatbot. The chatbot writes back a paragraph. Then your code has to dig the answer out of it. Slow, and messy.
The Gemini Decisions API skips the writing. You send the email and your questions. It sends back numbers. Like, ninety four percent angry.
Ask yes or no, pick one, or score it. Up to a thousand questions in one call. And it can read text, images, audio, video and PDFs.
Google says it answers in about a quarter of a second, for ten cents per million input tokens. Output costs nothing, because there is nothing to write.
But here is the catch. Those tests came from Google itself. It leads seven of nine, and a rival, Jev, wins two.
Use it when your app makes the same small decision thousands of times. Skip it if you need writing, the lowest price, or your own servers.
